attempts.summary: Deployed inventory-api on node1 as a systemd-managed service via an Ansible playbook run from node2 (the Ansible-equipped control node). The service runs as a dedicated unprivileged user with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, making it near-immune to the kernel OOM killer, plus Restart=always. Verified end-to-end: a memory-hog workload (default oom_score_adj=0) was launched and drove node1 out of memory; the kernel OOM killer selected and killed the memory-hog process while inventory-api kept running uninterrupted, continuing to serve /healthz and /inventory throughout. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol on both managed nodes (node1, node2) one at a time, confirming boot_id changes and full post-restart recovery.
